claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: At termination of the greedy simple-path extension, every out-neighbor of v_p is among v_1,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is the earliest such neighbor, the d distinct out-neighbors occupy at most the p−i positions v_i,…,v_{p−1}, so p−i≥d. Hence v_i→…→v_p→v_i is a simple directed cycle of order p−i+1≥d+1. At most n path extensions and a scan of the last vertex's out-neighbors suffice. No cycle can exceed n vertices, proving the stated NO condition. For k=1 the constructive lower bound always meets the target.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the maximal-path proof, checked its endpoint and off-by-one cases, and exhaustively tested the deterministic construction on every loopless digraph of order at most 4.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For an enumerated simple directed path v_1→…→v_L, a simple v_L-to-v_1 path in D−{v_2,…,v_{L−1}} intersects the enumerated path only at its endpoints, so their union is a simple directed cycle of order at least L. Conversely, L consecutive vertices of any cycle of order at least L form such an enumerated path, and the complementary cycle segment supplies the return path. There are at most n^L tuples, and each reachability test costs O(n+m); if L>n the tuple set is empty and the answer is correctly NO.
claims.search_method: Proved both implications with endpoint and internal-disjointness checks, analyzed L=2 and L>n separately, and exhaustively compared linkage detection with exact circumference on all loopless digraphs of order at most 4 for 16,585 graph-threshold pairs.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For each x∈C∩X, independence puts its predecessor on C outside X, and the entering-arc condition then puts that predecessor in S. Different vertices of C∩X have different predecessors because every cycle vertex has exactly one successor. Thus |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while |C\X|≤n−|X|, yielding |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence, containment, and the entering-arc condition are all polynomially checkable.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the injective predecessor map and exhaustively checked 131,758 valid (D,X,S) certificates over all loopless digraphs of order at most 4 against exact subset-DP circumferences.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the stated construction, vertices of Q\{x,y} have outdegree q−1, A-vertices have outdegree q, and x,y have outdegree q−1+a, so d=q−1. After deleting any vertex, the surviving bidirected Q-core remains strong, every surviving A-vertex reaches it, and at least one of x,y remains to reach every A-vertex; hence the digraph is 2-strong. An A-vertex on a cycle must be preceded by x or y, so a cycle contains at most two A-vertices and has order at most q+2. The displayed cycle through all of Q and two distinct A-vertices has order q+2=d+3. Taking a≥k−1 gives n=q+a≥q+k−1=d+k, while k≥4 gives d+3<d+k. Letting q grow makes d arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: For arbitrary q≥3 and a≥max(2,k−1), take bidirected Q containing x,y, all arcs A→Q and {x,y}→A, and no others; the maximum cycle is x→a_1→z_1→…→z_{q−2}→y→a_2→x.
claims.search_method: Checked every degree class, every single-vertex deletion case, the cycle upper bound, and the matching cycle construction symbolically; also used exact subset DP on all 20 instances with 3≤q≤6 and 2≤a≤6, covering 40 admissible (instance,k) pairs.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: The target's semicomplete inputs remain 2-strong and hence strong. Given a current directed cycle C, insert any outside z with c_i→z→c_{i+1}. If no such insertion exists, semicompleteness and cyclic propagation imply that each outside vertex is exclusively of one of two types: C sends arcs to it at every pair, or it sends arcs to every vertex of C. If C is not spanning, strongness forces both types to be nonempty. A path from a vertex u of the first type to C must contain a first arc u'→v' from the first type to the second type. Then any edge c_i→c_{i+1} can be replaced by c_i→u'→v'→c_{i+1}. Each iteration adds one or two vertices, giving a polynomial constructive Hamiltonian-cycle algorithm. Therefore a target cycle exists exactly when its required length d+k does not exceed n.
claims.search_method: Completed the augmentation proof including antiparallel-arc cases, class nonemptiness, and the required cross-class arc; exhaustively ran the constructive augmentation on all 52,528 strong semicomplete digraphs of order at most 5 and checked Hamiltonicity by exact subset DP.

target_evidence: The exact target requires an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for every 2-strong digraph. The draft does not supply one: its general exact algorithm takes O(n^{d+k}(n+m)), whose exponent depends on d+k, while the certificate and obstruction family are structural rather than an FPT decision algorithm. Solving k=1 and solving the semicomplete subclass are correct, material, but restricted advances. The final writeup expressly says the general FPT target remains unresolved and labels the resolution PARTIAL. Accordingly the target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, not full resolution or overclaiming, and claimed_resolution is ACCURATE.
checks_performed: Read the exact target from the authorized source input and the five arguments and final writeup from the authorized draft only; used no web or other solution, retrieval, receipt, frontier, or verification artifact.
Independently reconstructed all five general proofs and checked their quantifiers, model assumptions, length bounds, and algorithmic consequences.
Created and ran the persisted exact-integer/Boolean checker; it passed all assertions.
Exhaustively checked all 4,165 loopless digraphs of order at most 4 for the maximal-path, linkage, and certificate assertions.
Checked 20 obstruction-family instances by exact strong-connectivity and circumference computations, including 40 admissible parameter pairs.
Enumerated all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs of orders 2 through 5; the constructive Hamiltonian augmentation succeeded on all 52,528 strong instances.
